## Change

Catalog submission/update/withdrawal or contract/tooling change:

## Stable identity and release

- Block ID (preserved from the runtime manifest):
- Name / website slug:
- Creator GitHub handle/profile / current publisher if different / contributors:
- Source repository link (separate from profile):
- Release version / tested minimum OS:
- Public source repository / immutable commit / package folder:
- New listing, update or withdrawal (link existing listing):

## Runtime and distribution

- QML / hybrid / TUI; host Design API and custom components:
- Declared capabilities and why each is needed:
- Included files, indirect/dynamic assets and dependency providers:
- Third-party sources, revisions, licenses/notices and checksums:
- Private/local modifications excluded or intentionally released:
- Data migration/update/rollback limitations:

## Evidence

- [ ] I own this identity/source or have documented submission authority.
- [ ] Creator GitHub/profile and source links are retained; distinct publisher/contributors are credited without claiming endorsement.
- [ ] Public listing and source manifest agree on ID, version and permissions.
- [ ] Public source access and actual open-source license were checked.
- [ ] No private files, settings, credentials or private URLs are submitted.
- [ ] `npm test`, `npm run validate`, `npm run validate:contracts` pass.
- [ ] Local `validate:block -- ... --listing ...` passed (or explain why not applicable).
- Native preview / dependencies / install-reinstall checks actually run:
- Checks not run and known limitations:

Maintainer: review ownership, source, release continuity, capabilities and actual
evidence before merge. A metadata check/merge is not package signing, sandboxing
or a safety certificate. Merge makes a listing eligible for a later website
sync/build; it does not deploy or install it.
